summary: Appeal by the original informant (brother of deceased) against High Court's order suspending life imprisonment sentence and granting bail to three convicts pending appeal. Trial Court found respondents guilty of murdering Manish Kumar, the deceased, in furtherance of common intention based on eyewitness accounts and prosecution evidence. The murder allegedly occurred due to political rivalry following election of the deceased as Block Pramukh. High Court suspended sentence and granted bail; appellant challenged this, contending gravity of offence and risk of influence. Supreme Court examined standards for suspending sentence in murder cases and emphasized seriousness of offence.
